title: How many separate trees can you count in each of these?
question: In each strip, how many separate trees can you count? A number for each is the whole answer. If some merge and some do not, say roughly how many read as their own tree.
context_md:
**Calibrating a metric against your eye — not asking whether it looks good.**

`open-bugs-handoff.md` §Z says the stand reads as one mass, and that no metric could fail for it: the old one (widest unbroken run of plant cells) reported success on the very picture you rejected. Two replacements are now built. Before I trust either, they have to agree with what you actually see.

All three strips: same species, same soil, same frame (28,800), same 512-wide world. **Only the spacing between the planted trees differs.** Nothing about the plants themselves changed between them.

I have deliberately **not** said how many were planted in each — that is exactly what would bias a count.

What I already measured, and where I am unsure: my metric calls A a single fused mass and C fully separate. **B is the one I cannot call**, and it is the one that decides whether the number is usable at all.
